conclusion:
NO-CAP TEST (BETACRAFT_MAX_DURATION_MULT=99, every unit gets ~29.8s, ~the model's own max_length 2610). 3 sentences that hit the 2.5x cap earlier the same day; 1 died on MPS OOM.
RESULT: no bad audio shipped, but NOT because the runaway stopped happening. The Marathi countdown still ran away on attempt 1 — it was caught by the TAIL-FLUX detector instead (flux 0.018 < 0.030, a held vowel), reseeded, and came back at 1.01x. English with Mary was clean first attempt.
READING: the cap does not CAUSE the defect, it bounds the cost of it. Without the cap the bad attempt ran ~195s instead of ~131s — roughly 50% more GPU per failure. Tail flux is a genuine backstop but only for held-vowel endings; a runaway ending in noise has high flux and would slip past it. The two detectors are complementary, not redundant.
